questions.evidence:
Ronan finishes a class presentation and feels relieved when the final slide appears. He has memorized every sentence. Then a classmate asks how his recommendation would change if the budget were smaller. Ronan looks back at the slide, but the exact answer is not written there.

His teacher gives him time to think. Ronan identifies the recommendation's purpose and the two costs that mattered most. He says which part he would keep first and which part would need a cheaper alternative. He also names a price he would have to check before deciding.

The answer is less smooth than his prepared speech, but it shows how he connects information. After class, Ronan adds a page of possible questions to his notes. He does not try to memorize every imaginable reply. He practices explaining the reasons behind his choices so he can use them when a new condition appears.
